jobs.title: Director, Capital Investment & Decision Support
jobs.description:
Turner & Townsend is a global professional services company with over 22,000 people in more than 60 countries.

Working with our clients across real estate, infrastructure, energy and natural resources, we transform together delivering outcomes that improve people’s lives. Working in partnership makes it possible to deliver the world’s most impactful projects and programmes as we turn challenge into opportunity and complexity into success.

Our capabilities include programme, project, cost, asset and commercial management, controls and performance, procurement and supply chain, net zero and digital solutions.

We are majority-owned by CBRE Group, Inc., the world’s largest commercial real estate services and investment firm, with our partners holding a significant minority interest. Turner & Townsend and CBRE work together to provide clients with the premier programme, project and cost management offering in markets around the world.

Job Description

The Director, Capital Investment & Decision Support will lead and grow AMCL’s Capital Investment & Decision Support capability, working with asset-intensive organizations to improve how they plan, prioritize and make investment decisions across the asset lifecycle.

The role will combine senior client advisory, technical leadership, business development and team leadership. It will support clients across Infrastructure and Energy & Natural Resources to establish practical, evidence-based approaches to asset investment planning, lifecycle decision-making, risk, value and portfolio prioritization.

The Director will work closely with AMCL and Turner & Townsend colleagues across asset management, program and project delivery, controls, cost and commercial management, digital and data, bringing these capabilities together where clients require integrated solution

Lead complex client engagements focused on asset investment planning, lifecycle planning, capital prioritization, value-based decision-making and portfolio optimization.

Develop and apply decision-support frameworks that bring together cost, risk, performance, value and service outcomes to support transparent and defensible investment decisions.

jobs.description:
Senior Regional Vice President

Detailed Job Description

Job Overview

The Senior Regional Vice President (SRVP) is responsible for leading and managing overall business operations, market development, strategic execution, and organizational management within a designated region, ensuring that regional operational goals align with the company’s overarching strategic direction. This role entails comprehensive oversight of regional business performance, operational management, financial results, market expansion, client relations, and team development. The SRVP drives sustainable growth within the region while ensuring that all business activities comply with company policies, standards, and management requirements.

The SRVP works closely with the CEO, COO, CFO, other regional leaders, and the corporate executive team to formulate regional development strategies, facilitate cross-regional resource coordination, oversee the execution of major business initiatives, and resolve critical operational issues. Furthermore, the SRVP is responsible for cultivating regional management talent, optimizing operational systems, and enhancing market competitiveness to ensure long-term, stable business growth and operational success within the assigned region.

Key Responsibilities

I. Regional Strategic Planning and Leadership

Develop and implement long-term development strategies and annual operational plans for the assigned region, ensuring that regional objectives are aligned with the company’s overall strategy, financial goals, and market development direction. Analyze the regional market environment, industry trends, competitive landscape, and customer needs to identify new business opportunities and potential risks. Establish regional management standards and execution mechanisms, define the responsibilities, objectives, and performance requirements for each business unit, and drive the effective implementation of regional strategies.

II. Regional Business Operations and Performance Management

Provide comprehensive oversight of the daily operations of all business departments, branches, and operational units within the region, ensuring that business processes run efficiently and meet established performance targets. Regularly review revenue performance, operational efficiency, service quality, customer satisfaction, and business growth; identify operational deviations promptly and develop corrective measures. Coordinate activities across different departments within the region to resolve significant issues that impact business execution and operational efficiency.

III. Financial Management and Operational Goal Control

Oversee regional budget development, financial planning, cost control, and the analysis of operational results, ensuring that regional financial objectives align with the company’s overall financial plan. Collaborate with the CFO and the finance team to review regional revenue, profit, operating expenses, cash flow, and return on investment (ROI). Establish mechanisms for monitoring budget execution and financial performance; control operating costs effectively; enhance the efficiency of regional resource utilization; and ensure that all business units achieve their established financial objectives.

IV. Market Expansion and Business Growth

Lead regional market development, business expansion, and commercial growth initiatives, identifying potential customer segments, emerging markets, and strategic partnership opportunities. Oversee the development of sales channels, customer acquisition, marketing campaigns, and business collaborations to drive the growth of regional market share and enhance corporate brand influence. Partner with business development, sales, and marketing teams to formulate market-entry strategies and customer growth plans, ensuring the sustained competitiveness of the regional business.

V. Organizational Management and Team Leadership

Responsible for establishing and refining the regional management structure, and overseeing the performance of regional department heads and senior management. Define team performance objectives, talent development programs, and succession plans for management roles to strengthen regional organizational capabilities and the execution proficiency of the leadership team. Foster a positive corporate culture and cross-departmental collaboration, ensuring that managers at all levels effectively implement company policies, operational goals, and management requirements.

VI. Customer Relations and Strategic Partnership Management

Oversee the management of key regional customer relationships, strategic partnerships, and major commercial contracts, ensuring timely responses to customer needs and the stability of collaborative ties. Participate in negotiations with major clients, business collaborations, and the drafting and review of critical business agreements; coordinate the resolution of significant customer complaints, service disputes, and partnership-related issues. Collaborate with customer success, sales, and operations teams to improve customer satisfaction, retention rates, and long-term partnership value.

VII. Risk Management and Compliance Oversight

Monitor operational, financial, legal, and market risks within regional business activities, and establish effective mechanisms for risk identification, assessment, and mitigation. Ensure that all regional business units comply with applicable laws, industry regulations, internal corporate policies, and regulatory requirements. Work with legal, compliance, finance, and internal audit teams to periodically review regional management processes and internal controls, addressing significant compliance issues promptly and driving the implementation of corrective actions.

VIII. Communication with Senior Management and Strategic Execution

Provide regular reports to the CEO, COO, and the corporate executive management team regarding regional operational performance, market developments, financial results, business risks, and the progress of strategic plan execution. Provide management counsel regarding regional expansion, organizational restructuring, major investments, and business transformation. Facilitate the sharing of resources and information between various regions and corporate headquarters, ensure the unified execution of corporate strategy at the regional level, and drive long-term, sustainable growth for regional operations.

Qualifications

Education

Bachelor’s degree or higher in Business Administration, Management, Marketing, Financial Management, Economics, or a related field.

A Master of Business Administration (MBA) or a postgraduate degree in a relevant field is preferred.

Prior training in areas such as corporate operations management, strategic planning, financial management, or leadership is an advantage.

Proficiency in corporate management, regional market strategy, budget management, and risk control principles.

Work Experience

At least 20 years of professional experience in corporate management, business operations, market expansion, or regional management.

At least 7 years of experience in senior management or regional leadership roles.

Proven, hands-on experience in managing multiple business units, branches, or cross-regional operational teams.

A successful track record in developing regional business strategies, managing budgets, driving business growth, and enhancing operational performance.

Experience in managing cross-regional operations, or working within large-scale or multinational corporate environments, is preferred.

jobs.title: Chief Financial Officer
jobs.description:
Our client is a highly respected, mission-driven not-for-profit organization dedicated to improving well-being and quality of life in the communities it serves. The organization is seeking a strategic and forward-thinking Chief Financial Officer (CFO) to join its Executive Leadership Team. Reporting to the CEO, the CFO will provide enterprise-wide leadership across Finance and corporate services, while serving as a trusted advisor to the CEO, Board of Directors, and senior leadership team.

The organization delivers essential services to a large and diverse client base. Behind every service are countless financial, operational, and strategic decisions that turn resources into meaningful impact. As CFO, the successful candidate will ensure the financial strength, insight, and discipline needed to advance the mission and support long-term sustainability.

This is an exceptional opportunity for an accomplished finance executive who combines strategic insight with operational leadership and wants to influence meaningful outcomes in a purpose-driven organization. More than a functional leader, the CFO will be a key enterprise partner, helping shape strategy, support growth, and position the organization for continued success in a complex operating environment.

The Mandate

The mandate extends well beyond traditional financial stewardship. As a member of the Executive Leadership Team, the CFO will help shape organizational strategy, support evidence-based decision-making, and ensure the long-term sustainability of an organization delivering critical services.

In partnership with the CEO, Board, and senior leadership team, the CFO will provide strategic financial leadership across planning, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, treasury, audit, risk management, and compliance. They will ensure financial resources are aligned with organizational priorities while maintaining the discipline and accountability the mission requires.

A key priority will be supporting the organization through a period of growth and change. Using financial insights and performance data, the CFO will help evaluate opportunities, inform strategic initiatives, and optimize the deployment of resources in a complex funding and operating environment. Success will require balancing long-term vision with disciplined execution and sound financial management.

Beyond finance, the CFO will provide executive oversight of key corporate services, including procurement and facilities, ensuring effective stewardship of organizational resources and infrastructure. The role will also lead efforts to strengthen internal capabilities, foster collaboration across departments, and build a high-performing, engaged team.

The successful candidate will have the opportunity to evolve the finance function from a trusted service provider into an even more proactive strategic partner and to enable data-driven decision-making across the organization. Success will be measured not only by financial outcomes, but also by the ability to influence strategy, support growth, and contribute to long-term sustainability and impact.

Leadership and Stewardship

The organization is seeking a CFO who leads with maturity and earns trust through action. This is not a role for someone who relies on title or tenure to get things done. The culture here rewards people who show up prepared, communicate clearly, and follow through.
Operates with humility, credibility, and sound judgment

Experience working with Boards and senior executives in a strategic advisory capacity.
The ability to translate financial information into actionable business insights.
A collaborative leadership style and a reputation for building strong relationships across an organization.

Why This Role

This is a rare opportunity to combine executive-level impact with genuine purpose. As a strategic partner to the CEO and Executive Leadership Team, the CFO will help shape decisions that influence the organization’s direction, sustainability, and growth.

The successful candidate will join an organization at an exciting point in its journey, with the opportunity to strengthen financial stewardship, support strategic priorities, and help position the organization for continued success. The organization measures its success not only by financial performance, but by the positive impact it has on the people and communities it serves.

SNDL is one of Canada’s leading and fastest-growing liquor and cannabis companies. As the country’s largest private-sector retailer, our portfolio includes well-known banners such as Wine and Beyond, Liquor Depot, Ace Liquor, Value Buds, Spiritleaf, and Cost Cannabis.

Driven by purpose, performance, and people, SNDL is shaping the future of retail and cannabis by bringing people together through exceptional products and experiences.

About the Role

Reporting to the Senior Vice President, Accounting and External Reporting, the Director leads the Company’s external reporting and consolidation activities. This senior, highly visible role is accountable for accurate and timely IFRS reporting, disciplined monthly consolidation, regulatory compliance, audit coordination and the integrity of financial information provided to senior leadership and external stakeholders. The Director works independently, applies sound judgment, leads through change and partners across Finance and the broader organization.

Responsibilities

External Reporting and Regulatory Compliance

Lead the preparation of quarterly and annual consolidated IFRS financial statements, notes and Management’s Discussion and Analysis (MD&A), ensuring accuracy, consistency and clear disclosure of results, significant judgments and key business developments.
Manage internal, legal, executive and external-auditor review comments through final approval and filing, maintaining clear ownership, version control and supporting documentation.
Coordinate preparation of the annual report and support applicable Canadian and U.S. securities and regulatory filings, including disclosure and XBRL requirements where applicable.
Oversee the financial review, approval and filing of Company press releases and website updates to ensure consistency with publicly disclosed financial information.
Monitor changes in IFRS and regulatory requirements; assess reporting impacts and partner with Technical Accounting to implement new standards and update policies and disclosures.
Prepare financial reporting and Audit Committee materials, as required, and respond to requests from senior leaders and other stakeholders.
Provide senior-level leadership to the external reporting and consolidation function, setting priorities, coaching team members and promoting accountability, quality and continuous improvement.

Consolidation and Management Reporting

Lead the monthly, quarterly and annual consolidation process across legal entities and reportable segments, including trial-balance aggregation, eliminations, top-side entries, foreign currency translation and the consolidation of an equity-accounted joint venture.
Prepare monthly consolidated and key segment reports, including income statement and cash flow reporting, for the Senior Leadership Team (SLT). Explain corporate items, material variances and key drivers during monthly finance reviews.
Prepare and maintain monthly consolidated trial-balance uploads for FP&A reporting. Own the reconciliation of internal management reporting to external results and safeguard data integrity across reporting platforms.
Review intercompany reconciliations, consolidation workbooks, cash flow support, earnings-per-share schedules and other quarterly reporting workbooks for accuracy, completeness and appropriate evidence of review.
Prepare or review share-based compensation, share capital and related monthly journal entries and continuity schedules.

Audit, Controls and Governance

Act as a primary contact for external auditors. Coordinate quarterly reviews and the annual audit, manage timelines and deliverables, resolve issues promptly and ensure complete supporting documentation.
Develop, maintain and improve SOX-compliant internal controls over financial reporting, including control documentation, evidence standards, deficiency remediation and readiness for testing.
Maintain robust financial reporting policies, procedures, reconciliations and review controls that support reliable and repeatable reporting outcomes.
Lead the integration of financial reporting data from acquired businesses, including mapping, consolidation, reporting calendars, controls and alignment of accounting policies and standards.

Leadership, Integration and Continuous Improvement

Partner with FP&A, Corporate Accounting, Tax, Treasury, Legal, Investor Relations, business finance teams and information technology to deliver consistent financial information and resolve cross-functional issues.
Drive change by simplifying consolidation and reporting processes, strengthening data governance and advancing automation and scalable reporting solutions while preserving control integrity.
Lead special projects involving complex transactions, acquisitions, dispositions, financing activities and reporting-system implementations.

Qualifications

CPA designation with 15+ years of progressive experience and proven record in financial reporting, consolidation or audit, including leadership experience in a complex public-company environment.
Experience with Regulatory reporting requirements – SEDAR and EDGAR
Advanced knowledge of IFRS, consolidated financial statements, MD&A, securities reporting, internal controls and SOX requirements; familiarity with U.S. regulatory reporting is a strong asset.
Experience leading multi-entity and multi-segment consolidations, intercompany eliminations, foreign currency translation, equity accounting, cash flow reporting and share-based compensation.
Experience coordinating external audits and working with executive leadership, Audit Committees, legal counsel and other external advisors.
Experience with acquisitions, financial data integration, reporting transformation and consolidation or disclosure-management systems. Advanced Microsoft Excel skills are required; experience with ERP, Power BI and Workiva or similar tools is an asset.

Required Competencies

Senior-level leadership and sound professional judgment
Exceptional attention to detail and commitment to accuracy
Ability to work independently, prioritize competing demands and meet tight deadlines
Clear, concise written and verbal communication
Change leadership, process improvement and systems mindset

What Makes SNDL a Great Place to Grow:

Competitive compensation including performance-based bonuses and annual salary reviews.
Comprehensive health and dental benefits, including a Healthcare Spending Account.
Three weeks of paid vacation with annual rollover.
Flexible, hybrid work arrangements to support work-life balance.
Recognition and rewards programs that celebrate individual and team achievements.
Employee & Family Assistance Program (EFAP) with mental health, financial, and family support.
Employee perks and discounts program, offering savings across fitness, wellness, lifestyle, retail, and everyday services

We are grateful for the interest in this role from all candidates, however, we will be contacting only those that are selected for next steps in the hiring process.

Our Commitment to Diversity & Inclusion

SNDL is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a welcoming, inclusive, diverse and safe workplace where all of our team members have equal opportunity to succeed. We know this begins with recruitment. To honor our commitment, SNDL encourages applications from individuals of all backgrounds, sexual orientation, gender identity, ancestry, ages and abilities.

Targeted compensation - $145,000 - $155,000

About SNDL

SNDL is one of Canada’s leading and fastest-growing liquor and cannabis companies. As the country’s largest private-sector retailer, our portfolio includes well-known banners such as Wine and Beyond, Liquor Depot, Ace Liquor, Value Buds, Spiritleaf, and Cost Cannabis.

We’re also one of Canada’s largest vertically integrated cannabis producers, recognized for our innovation, low-cost manufacturing, and award-winning brands including Top Leaf, Contraband, Palmetto, Bon Jak, La Plogue, Versus, Grasslands, Vacay, Pearls by Grön, No Future, and Bhang Chocolate.

Driven by purpose, performance, and people, SNDL is shaping the future of retail and cannabis by bringing people together through exceptional products and experiences.

About the Role

Reporting to the Senior Vice President, Accounting and External Reporting, the Director leads the Company’s external reporting and consolidation activities. This senior, highly visible role is accountable for accurate and timely IFRS reporting, disciplined monthly consolidation, regulatory compliance, audit coordination and the integrity of financial information provided to senior leadership and external stakeholders. The Director works independently, applies sound judgment, leads through change and partners across Finance and the broader organization.

Responsibilities

External Reporting and Regulatory Compliance

Lead the preparation of quarterly and annual consolidated IFRS financial statements, notes and Management’s Discussion and Analysis (MD&A), ensuring accuracy, consistency and clear disclosure of results, significant judgments and key business developments.
Manage internal, legal, executive and external-auditor review comments through final approval and filing, maintaining clear ownership, version control and supporting documentation.
Coordinate preparation of the annual report and support applicable Canadian and U.S. securities and regulatory filings, including disclosure and XBRL requirements where applicable.
Oversee the financial review, approval and filing of Company press releases and website updates to ensure consistency with publicly disclosed financial information.
Monitor changes in IFRS and regulatory requirements; assess reporting impacts and partner with Technical Accounting to implement new standards and update policies and disclosures.
Prepare financial reporting and Audit Committee materials, as required, and respond to requests from senior leaders and other stakeholders.
Provide senior-level leadership to the external reporting and consolidation function, setting priorities, coaching team members and promoting accountability, quality and continuous improvement.

Consolidation and Management Reporting

Lead the monthly, quarterly and annual consolidation process across legal entities and reportable segments, including trial-balance aggregation, eliminations, top-side entries, foreign currency translation and the consolidation of an equity-accounted joint venture.
Prepare monthly consolidated and key segment reports, including income statement and cash flow reporting, for the Senior Leadership Team (SLT). Explain corporate items, material variances and key drivers during monthly finance reviews.
Prepare and maintain monthly consolidated trial-balance uploads for FP&A reporting. Own the reconciliation of internal management reporting to external results and safeguard data integrity across reporting platforms.
Review intercompany reconciliations, consolidation workbooks, cash flow support, earnings-per-share schedules and other quarterly reporting workbooks for accuracy, completeness and appropriate evidence of review.
Prepare or review share-based compensation, share capital and related monthly journal entries and continuity schedules.

Audit, Controls and Governance

Act as a primary contact for external auditors. Coordinate quarterly reviews and the annual audit, manage timelines and deliverables, resolve issues promptly and ensure complete supporting documentation.
Develop, maintain and improve SOX-compliant internal controls over financial reporting, including control documentation, evidence standards, deficiency remediation and readiness for testing.
Maintain robust financial reporting policies, procedures, reconciliations and review controls that support reliable and repeatable reporting outcomes.
Lead the integration of financial reporting data from acquired businesses, including mapping, consolidation, reporting calendars, controls and alignment of accounting policies and standards.

Leadership, Integration and Continuous Improvement

Partner with FP&A, Corporate Accounting, Tax, Treasury, Legal, Investor Relations, business finance teams and information technology to deliver consistent financial information and resolve cross-functional issues.
Drive change by simplifying consolidation and reporting processes, strengthening data governance and advancing automation and scalable reporting solutions while preserving control integrity.
Lead special projects involving complex transactions, acquisitions, dispositions, financing activities and reporting-system implementations.

Qualifications

CPA designation with 15+ years of progressive experience and proven record in financial reporting, consolidation or audit, including leadership experience in a complex public-company environment.
Experience with Regulatory reporting requirements – SEDAR and EDGAR
Advanced knowledge of IFRS, consolidated financial statements, MD&A, securities reporting, internal controls and SOX requirements; familiarity with U.S. regulatory reporting is a strong asset.
Experience leading multi-entity and multi-segment consolidations, intercompany eliminations, foreign currency translation, equity accounting, cash flow reporting and share-based compensation.
Experience coordinating external audits and working with executive leadership, Audit Committees, legal counsel and other external advisors.
Experience with acquisitions, financial data integration, reporting transformation and consolidation or disclosure-management systems. Advanced Microsoft Excel skills are required; experience with ERP, Power BI and Workiva or similar tools is an asset.

Required Competencies

Senior-level leadership and sound professional judgment
Exceptional attention to detail and commitment to accuracy
Ability to work independently, prioritize competing demands and meet tight deadlines
Clear, concise written and verbal communication
Change leadership, process improvement and systems mindset

What Makes SNDL a Great Place to Grow:

Competitive compensation including performance-based bonuses and annual salary reviews.
Comprehensive health and dental benefits, including a Healthcare Spending Account.
Three weeks of paid vacation with annual rollover.
Flexible, hybrid work arrangements to support work-life balance.
Recognition and rewards programs that celebrate individual and team achievements.
Employee & Family Assistance Program (EFAP) with mental health, financial, and family support.
Employee perks and discounts program, offering savings across fitness, wellness, lifestyle, retail, and everyday services

We are grateful for the interest in this role from all candidates, however, we will be contacting only those that are selected for next steps in the hiring process.

Our Commitment to Diversity & Inclusion

SNDL is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to building a welcoming, inclusive, diverse and safe workplace where all of our team members have equal opportunity to succeed. We know this begins with recruitment. To honor our commitment, SNDL encourages applications from individuals of all backgrounds, sexual orientation, gender identity, ancestry, ages and abilities.
